expectations.text: Explicitly states that unanchored MaxDiff utilities cannot support absolute importance claims
expectations.evidence: 'The only valid claim from unanchored MaxDiff is: Item A is more preferred than Item B. You cannot claim Item A is important or Item B is unimportant.' Also: 'Do not present unanchored utilities with language like moderately important or low importance... it is just labeling arbitrary points on a relative scale.'

expectations.text: Recommends direct binary anchor as the default approach
expectations.evidence: 'Direct binary anchor (recommended default)' — explicitly labeled as such. Section describes post-MaxDiff checklist question with wording guidance.

expectations.text: Mentions dual-response anchor as an alternative
expectations.evidence: 'Dual-response anchor (use when direct binary would feel awkward)' — explicitly described as follow-up after each MaxDiff set, with pros and cons relative to direct binary.

expectations.text: Discusses reporting format (share-above-anchor, not just raw rescaled utility)
expectations.evidence: 'Share above the bar — the percentage of respondents for whom each item exceeded the threshold. This is the actually important number. Items at 70%+ are broadly important; items at 20% are niche or irrelevant.'

eval_feedback.overall: All assertions pass cleanly. Response is precise on direct binary vs dual-response distinction, which is a key differentiator from the baseline.
